sections.heading: Commercial Roof Replacement We Provide in Newark, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing replaces 6 commercial roof systems across Essex County: EPDM rubber, TPO, PVC, modified bitumen, built-up roofing, and standing-seam metal.

runs.v: Replacement accounts for 79.2% of US roofing installations in 2025, per Mordor Intelligence, driven by membrane age and storm loss rather than new construction.

c.v: EPDM membrane replacement

items.v: — New EPDM rubber lasts 15 to 25 years and fails most often at the splice seams, per the InterNACHI chart and NRCA technical guidance. It is ideal for low-slope and flat roofs, popular on Newark commercial buildings for its long lifespan and low maintenance, and fire-retardant grades add fire resistance.

c.v: TPO membrane replacement

items.v: — Heat-welded TPO has an effective service life of 7 to 20 years, per the InterNACHI chart, and is known for high solar reflectivity and durability. Sheets typically run 10 to 16 feet wide and up to 100 feet long; seam failures at the welds are its most common defect, per NRCA technical guidance.

c.v: PVC membrane replacement

items.v: — PVC lasts 20 to 30 years, per Single Ply Roofing Industry guidance. PVC membranes resist rooftop grease and chemicals, per Duro-Last product data, and white PVC blocks UV rays and reflects up to about 90% of the sun's energy when new, improving energy efficiency.

c.v: Modified bitumen and built-up replacement

items.v: — Modified bitumen lasts 20 years, and built-up roofing, laid in hot asphalt, lasts well over 20 years with proper care, 30 years per the InterNACHI chart.

c.v: Tear-off and deck repair

items.v: — Multiple layers mean a tear-off rather than a recover: N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires full removal of a water-soaked roof or one with 2 or more layers. Serious structural issues in the roof deck are fixed first, since the deck carries the structural load of the insulation and roofing system.

c.v: Tapered insulation and drainage correction

items.v: — Proper drainage slope is critical on commercial roofing systems: tapered insulation builds at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to clear ponding water, which counts as a defect after 48 hours, per the NRCA and ARMA.

sections.heading: How Often Does a Commercial Roof Need to Be Replaced?

c.v: Most commercial membranes need replacement every 15 to 30 years, TPO sometimes sooner, while standing-seam metal roofing lasts 40 to 70 years depending on the material.

runs.v: Newark's estimated 30–50 freeze-thaw cycles each winter, humid summers, and heavy rain favor durable roofing materials with thermal resistance, and insufficient moisture management shortens any roofing system's life.

Regular commercial roof maintenance reaches the long end: experts recommend annual roof inspections, and many commercial roofers set scheduled inspections each spring and fall to check membranes, seams, flashing, and drainage and catch minor issues before they worsen. Timely roof repairs prevent more expensive repairs; proper maintenance is the cheapest long-term protection.

sections.heading: Commercial Roof Repair or Replacement? The 25% Rule and Cost-Effective Choices

c.v: The 25% rule for roofing is a code threshold: in New Jersey, repairing up to 25% of a commercial roof's area in 12 months is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and major work beyond that, including replacement, needs a permit.

runs.v: Past 25 to 30% damage, a new roof usually beats more roof repairs, while a recover over one dry layer can be one of the more cost-effective solutions where code allows.
A comprehensive roof inspection is essential before choosing between a commercial roof repair and replacement, and prompt fixes avoid costly repairs.

sections.heading: Our Commercial Roof Replacement Process, Step by Step

items.v: Moisture Survey and Building Assessment
A Newark Quality Roofing technician makes the initial assessment of the deck, insulation, and drainage, including an ASTM C1153 moisture survey.
System Specification and Written Estimate
A Newark Quality Roofing written estimate sets scope, labor, materials, and timeline; detailed estimates that specify the roofing assembly and warranty are what transparent pricing looks like.
Permit and Project Planning
A Newark Quality Roofing crew files the permit N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 requires, phases the work around weather conditions, and coordinates with building operations for minimal disruption.
Tear-Off and Deck Repair
The crew strips the covering in managed sections and repairs deteriorated decking and any structural damage, restoring structural integrity.
Insulation, Drainage, and Membrane Installation
The crew installs staggered rigid insulation, builds tapered insulation to ¼ inch per foot, and installs the membrane to manufacturer specification.
Verification, Closeout, and Warranty
A Newark Quality Roofing lead verifies seams, flashing, and drainage, registers the manufacturer system warranty, and issues a written workmanship warranty on the labor.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace your commercial roof?

runs.v: Replace it when damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof, leaks recur in one spot, or core samples show saturated insulation across most of the roof; otherwise repair.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial roof replacement in Newark, NJ?

runs.v: Yes. Only repairs to up to 25% of the roof area in 12 months are exempt, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

faqs.q: What is the typical lifespan of a new commercial roof?

runs.v: Most membranes last 15 to 30 years (TPO 7 to 20), and standing-seam metal lasts 40 to 70.

faqs.q: How much does commercial roof replacement cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Single-ply typically runs $7.00 to $12.00 per square foot installed in New Jersey; Newark Quality Roofing provides a free written estimate.

faqs.q: Is $30,000 too much for a roof?

runs.v: It is high for a typical Newark house, where replacement is commonly quoted at $8,500 to $17,000, unless the roof is large or slate. On a commercial roof, $30,000 covers only about 2,500 to 4,300 square feet of single-ply.

faqs.q: Should you add insulation during a commercial roof replacement?

runs.v: Yes: rigid insulation goes under the new membrane, and tapered insulation builds at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to clear ponding water.

faqs.q: How does an infrared moisture survey scope a commercial roof replacement?

runs.v: An ASTM C1153 survey reads wet insulation, which holds heat longer, as a warm anomaly after sunset; core cuts in the affected areas confirm it.

faqs.q: How does a commercial roof replacement handle the Essex County winter?

runs.v: A Newark Quality Roofing replacement seam-bonds the membrane and builds positive drainage for winters that cross 32°F repeatedly.

faqs.q: Do commercial roofers handle emergency roof repairs for urgent commercial roofing needs?

runs.v: Yes. Active leaks require immediate emergency roof repairs, a critical local service, even on a roof slated for replacement: tarping and securing damaged areas prevents further damage and can often be completed within a couple of hours. Newark Quality Roofing emergency crews are available 24/7 and target a 1–4 hour emergency response.

faqs.q: Does an expert team handle the permit and final inspection?

runs.v: Yes. Newark Quality Roofing files the construction permit, and the final inspection verifies compliance with New Jersey's Uniform Construction Code, which Newark roofing contractors must follow.
